item.title: Maná Will Fire Up Mexico vs. England Match With Halftime Show: ‘Get Ready to Sing at the Top of Your Lungs’
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: "Welcome to our podcast, where we're always on top of the latest trends and news in music. Today, we're talking about the iconic Mexican band Maná, who are set to take the stage at the Estadio Ciudad de México, formerly known as Estadio Azteca, this Sunday, July 5th, for a halftime show like no other."
[Upbeat music transitions in]
Host: "Maná will be performing during the highly anticipated match between Mexico and England, as they compete for a spot in the quarterfinals of the World Cup. The band announced the news on social media, inviting fans to sing along at the top of their lungs. And with their music, you know it's going to be a wild ride."
[Short clip of Maná's music plays]
Host: "This performance will mark the end of Maná's historic run at the FIFA World Cup 2026. They previously participated in the tournament's opening ceremony on June 11th, sharing the stage with stars like Shakira and J Balvin, and captivating a global audience of 1.1 billion viewers."
[Music transitions to a more energetic beat]
Host: "And in a fun twist, lead singer Fher Olvera recently responded to Liam Gallagher's prediction that England would crush Mexico 5-0. Olvera had a few words of his own, saying '5-0? Calm down! We'll see what happens on Sunday, man.' The stage is set for an epic showdown, both on and off the field."
[Music slows down]
Host: "Maná has been making waves lately, with a free concert in Guadalajara that drew 170,000 attendees, and a world tour that's taking them to stadiums across Latin America. With over 50 million records sold, four Grammy Awards, and a career spanning four decades, Maná remains one of the most relevant Latin acts of all time."
[Outro music plays]
Host: "That's all for today's episode. Don't miss Maná's halftime show this Sunday, and get ready to sing along with one of the most iconic Latin rock bands of all time. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you on the next one."
